beats.speaker: Sifu, The Wise
beats.text:
Everything you have built so far, you believed in. Belief is not evidence.

This world exists to take your belief away and give you something better.

beats.speaker: Sifu, The Wise
beats.text: The Regression Dragon has one power, and it is enough: it makes old, dead bugs live again. Fix something here, and something you fixed three worlds ago breaks behind you.

beats.title: Testing shows presence, never absence
beats.body:
A passing test proves that one path, with one set of inputs, behaved as expected once.

It does not prove the system is correct. Dijkstra's line is the honest one: testing can show the presence of bugs, never their absence. This is not a reason to skip it — it is the reason to choose your tests deliberately rather than write many careless ones.

beats.title: The levels, smallest first
steps: Unit. One function or class, isolated from everything around it. Fast, precise, and where most tests should live.
Integration. Two or more parts together — does the code actually talk to the database it claims to?
System. The whole assembled thing, tested against what it was asked to do.
Acceptance. The stakeholder's own question: is this the thing I asked for? Reqoria's requirements are what this is checked against.
Regression. Run the old tests again. Not to find new bugs — to prove the old ones stayed dead.

beats.title: Two questions, both necessary
beats.left_body:
“Did we build the thing right?”

Against the specification. Unit tests, integration tests, code review.

Catches defects.
beats.right_body:
“Did we build the right thing?”

Against the actual need. Acceptance testing, user trials, demos.

Catches misunderstandings.

beats.title: What a good test asserts
beats.good:
def test_discount():
    assert apply_discount(100, 0.1) == 90
    assert apply_discount(0, 0.1) == 0
    with raises(ValueError):
        apply_discount(100, 1.5)
beats.verdict: The first passes for almost any broken implementation. The second pins the normal case, the boundary, and the refusal. A test that cannot fail is not a test — it is a comment that costs CPU time.

beats.title: Why regression exists at all
beats.body:
Software has no isolated changes. A fix alters shared state, a shared function, a shared assumption — and something far away that quietly relied on the old behaviour stops working.

A regression suite is the memory of every bug you have already paid for. Run automatically, on every change, it is the only thing standing between you and paying for them twice.

beats.question: You fix a bug in the login code. Which test should you run to catch damage done elsewhere?
options: Only the new test for the bug you fixed
A manual check of the login screen
beats.explanation: Correct answer: the full regression suite. The new test proves the bug is gone; it says nothing about what the fix broke. “The change was small” is the sentence that precedes most production incidents — size of diff and size of blast radius are unrelated.

beats.speaker: Sifu, The Wise
beats.text:
The Dragon cannot be killed by being clever once. It is killed by writing down what you learned, so the next version of you cannot forget it.

That is all an automated test is: a lesson that refuses to be unlearned.
